design.text: International, multicenter, randomized (2:1), double-blind, placebo-controlled study comparing siltuximab plus best supportive care (BSC) to placebo plus BSC, infused every 3 weeks; randomization stratified by concomitant corticosteroid use.

citations.quote: The indication was evaluated in an international, multicenter, randomized (2:1), phase 2 study of every 3 week infusions comparing Sylvant (siltuximab) and best supportive care (BSC) to placebo and BSC.
Patient randomization was stratified by concomitant corticosteroid use at study entry.

population.text: Patients with multicentric Castleman's disease (MCD) who are HIV-negative and HHV-8-negative.

citations.quote: This is an initial Biologic Licensing Application (BLA) seeking the approval of intravenous siltuximab for the treatment of patients with MCD who are human immunodeficiency virus negative and human herpesvirus-8 negative.

endpoint.text: Durable tumor and symptomatic response: tumor response (complete or partial by modified Cheson criteria) assessed by independent review plus complete resolution or stabilization of MCD symptoms, sustained for at least 18 weeks.

citations.quote: The major efficacy outcome of the study was durable tumor and symptomatic response, defined as tumor response (complete or partial response based on modified Cheson criteria) assessed by independent review and complete resolution or stabilization of MCD symptoms, sustained for at least 18 weeks.
The main study CNT0328MCD2001 supporting this application is a phase 2, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled study in 79 patients with MCD to assess the efficacy and safe
There were 53 patients randomized to the SYLVANT arm at a dosage of 11 mg/kg and 26 patients randomized to the placebo arm.

result.text: Durable tumor & symptomatic response rate 34% (18/53) with siltuximab vs 0% (0/26) with placebo (95% CI of difference 11.1, 54.8; p=0.0012). Tumor response 38% vs 4%; median time to treatment failure not reached vs 134 days (HR 0.418, 95% CI 0.21 to 0.82; p<0.05).

citations.quote: The response rate in the siltuximab group compared with the placebo group was 34% (18/53) versus 0% (0/26), (95% CI of the difference: 11.1, 54.8; p=0.0012).

The best tumor response in the siltuximab group compared with the placebo group was 38% (20/53) versus 4% (1/26), (95% CI of the difference: 11.1, 54.8; p < 0.05). The waterfall plot is presented as Figure 5. (copied from submission Study Report CNT0328MCD2001 page 91/766)

The median time to treatment failure was not reached in the siltuximab arm and was 134 days in the placebo arm. (HR 0.418, (95% CI of HR: 0.21 to 0.82; p < 0.05)). The Kaplan Meier analysis is presented in Figure 6. (copied from submission Study Report CNT0328MCD2001 page 96/766)

target_moa.text: Siltuximab is an interleukin-6 (IL-6) antagonist: it binds IL-6 and prevents its binding to soluble or membrane-bound IL-6 receptor, thereby inhibiting IL-6-related signaling. Excess IL-6 is implicated in the systemic manifestations of Castleman's disease.

citations.quote: Siltuximab binds to IL6 and prevents the binding of IL6 to the soluble or membrane bound IL6-receptor, thus inhibiting the IL-6 related signaling pathway. Based on its mechanism of action, the pharmacologic class assigned to siltuximab is "IL-6 antagonist"
Castleman's disease has been linked to excessive release of IL-6 or similar polypeptides.

modality.text: mAb — full-length recombinant chimeric (human-mouse) IgG1 kappa monoclonal antibody directed to IL-6.

citations.quote: Siltuximab (CINTO 328) is a full length recombinant chimeric (human-mouse) IgG1 kappa monoclonal antibody that is directed to interleukin-6 (IL-6), a proinflammatory cytokine.

key_safety.text: Most common adverse reactions (>10% of patients) were rash, pruritus, upper respiratory tract infection, increased weight, and hyperuricemia. In Study 1, rash occurred in 28% (vs 12% placebo), pruritus 28% (vs 8%), upper respiratory tract infection 26% (vs 15%), and edema 26% (vs 27%).
